home.description: Every week, month or season, your group gets a few questions. Everyone answers in their own time, and the answers come back as one issue you all read.

steps.title: Questions go out
steps.body: On the day you pick, everyone in the loop gets a few questions by email.

steps.title: Friends answer from the link
steps.body: Each person opens the link in their email and writes back, whenever suits them.

steps.title: Everyone gets the issue
steps.body: When the round closes, all the answers arrive together as one issue for the whole group.

home.noAccount: Your friends don't need an account or an app.

questionPacks.name: Everyday
questions: What made you laugh this week?
What are you looking forward to?
What's something small you're proud of?
What did you eat that was worth remembering?
What's the last thing that surprised you?
Who did you talk to this week that you want to see again?
Who's someone you've been thinking about lately?
What's something you'd like to thank someone for?
Where did you go that was worth the trip?
What's a place you keep meaning to visit?
What's been on your mind?
What did you change your mind about recently?
What's something you're bad at and enjoying anyway?

questionPacks.name: Travel
questions: What's a trip you still think about?
Where would you go with a free week and no plan?
What's the best thing you've eaten in another city?
What's a place near home that feels like a holiday?
Window seat or aisle, and why?
What did a trip teach you that stuck?
What's the worst travel day you'd happily repeat?
Which city would you move to for a month?
What do you always pack and never use?
Who would you take on a road trip tomorrow?

questionPacks.name: Food
questions: What did you cook that you'd make again?
What's your comfort meal after a long day?
What food did you hate as a kid and love now?
What's the best thing you ate this week?
What would your last meal on earth be?
What snack disappears fastest in your house?
What's a restaurant you keep going back to?
What food reminds you of someone you love?
What should the group cook together one day?
What did you eat standing up and still enjoy?

questionPacks.name: Childhood
questions: What did you want to be when you grew up?
What's a smell that takes you straight back?
What was your favorite thing to do after school?
What's a family tradition you'd keep forever?
What song did you play to death as a kid?
What did you believe that turned out to be wrong?
What's a small memory from childhood that still makes you smile?
What did you collect, and where is it now?
Who was your best friend at ten, and what made them great?
What would you tell your younger self on a Monday morning?

questionPacks.name: Friendship
questions: What did a friend do recently that meant a lot?
How do you show someone you're glad they exist?
What's the earliest memory you have with someone in this group?
Who makes you laugh the hardest?
What did friendship look like when you were twenty?
What do you want friends to ask you more often?
What's a tiny tradition you'd like to start with this group?
When did you last meet someone new and click right away?
What have you learned about being a friend lately?
What does a good catch-up look like for you?

questionPacks.name: Hot takes
questions: What's a harmless hill you'll die on?
Which everyday thing is wildly overrated?
What do you love that everyone else finds boring?
What's a food opinion that would upset a chef?
What's a small luxury worth every penny?
What's something popular you've never understood?
What's a rule you'd delete from the world?
What's your most stubborn take about breakfast?
What would you ban if you were briefly in charge?
What's the most overrated way to spend a weekend?

questionPacks.name: Books and films
questions: What did you read or watch recently that stayed with you?
What's a film you've seen more than twice?
Which character did you want to be as a kid?
What's a book you'd press into someone's hands?
What did you abandon halfway through, and why?
What's a comfort rewatch for a rainy day?
What song belongs in the soundtrack of your week?
Which fictional world would you visit for a day?
What did you love as a teenager and still defend?
What should the group's first watch party be?

questionPacks.name: Weekend plans
questions: What did last weekend actually look like?
What does a perfect Saturday morning look like?
What are you doing this weekend that you're looking forward to?
What's your favorite way to waste a Sunday?
What's a tiny plan that made a weekend better?
Who did you spend your weekend with, and what did you do?
What's a local thing everyone should do once?
What does your ideal doing-nothing day look like?
What did you put off last weekend and still didn't do?
What's the next thing you want to plan with friends?

questionPacks.name: Tiny joys
questions: What tiny thing made you unreasonably happy this week?
What small thing are you grateful for today?
What made you smile on your way somewhere?
What's the best thing that happened in your kitchen this week?
What's a little ritual that makes a normal day nicer?
What did you notice this week that you'd normally miss?
What song, snack, or moment lifted the week?
What's the nicest thing you saw someone else do?
What did you do slowly and enjoy more for it?
What tiny victory should we celebrate?

questionPacks.name: Creature comforts
questions: If your pet could text you once, what would it say?
What animal would be your spirit roommate?
What's an animal you relate to on Mondays?
What's the cutest thing you've seen this week?
What animal fact do you love telling people?
If you could be any animal for a day, which and why?
What's a creature you'd protect at all costs?
What does your ideal cozy night in look like?
What's the softest thing in your home?
What animal would win your group's talent show?

questionPacks.name: Friendship lore
questions: Who in the group is most likely to befriend a pigeon?
What's a story about this group that deserves retelling?
What did this group teach you about yourself?
What was your first impression of someone here, and how wrong was it?
Which group trip or day out should we relive?
What's a tradition this group accidentally started?
What would this group's theme song be?
What do you want us to remember about this year?
What's a compliment someone here gave you that stuck?
What should we do together that we haven't yet?

questionPacks.name: Silly hypotheticals
questions: Which household object would be your nemesis if it came alive?
If you had to replace your hands with something, what would you pick?
What would you name a boat if you had one tomorrow?
If your week were a weather forecast, what would it say?
What's the worst superpower you could be given?
If you could only eat one color of food, which color?
What would you put in a time capsule for this group?
If animals could talk, which would be the rudest?
What's a completely useless skill you'd love to have?
If tomorrow became a public holiday in your honor, what would it celebrate?

a11yLabels.removeMemberBody: They stop getting rounds. Their past answers stay in the issues they were part of.
a11yLabels.resetSharesBody: Links you already sent stop working, and new ones are made.
a11yLabels.archiveQuestionBody: It leaves the pool and stops being asked in future rounds.
a11yLabels.archiveSectionBody: It leaves this list and stops appearing in future issues.
a11yLabels.removeEventBody: The event is deleted for good and can't be brought back.

unsubscribe.title: Stop emails from {groupName}?
unsubscribe.body: You'll stay in the loop, and the answer link in your earlier emails keeps working. You just won't get questions, reminders or new rounds by email.
unsubscribe.mutedBody: You're still in the loop, and the answer link in your earlier emails still works. Changed your mind? Turn them back on.
unsubscribe.invalidBody: It may have been copied incompletely, or you're no longer in this loop.
unsubscribe.oneClickDone: Done. This loop won't email you any more; you're still in it.
unsubscribe.notice: You've turned off emails from this loop. You won't hear about new rounds unless you check back here.

devFeedback.title: Feedback
devFeedback.description: Everything sent from the corner button, newest first.
devFeedback.warning: Notes can carry names and email addresses. Keep this page to yourself.
devFeedback.empty: Nothing yet. Use the button in the corner of any page.

account.title: Delete your account
account.intro: This deletes your account and everything you have written in every loop: answers, photos, voice notes, comments, reactions, and suggested questions. Rounds that already went out will no longer show anything from you. It cannot be undone.
account.soloTitle: These loops have nobody else in them, so they go too:
account.blockedTitle: First, hand on or delete the loops you own
account.blockedBody: Other people are still in these loops. Make one of their admins the owner on the people page, or delete the loop from its settings, then come back.
account.confirmLabel: Type your email address to confirm
account.confirmError: That doesn't match your email address. Nothing was deleted.
account.ownerError: You still own a loop with other people in it. Nothing was deleted.

leave.title: Leave {groupName}?
leave.body: You will stop getting emails from this loop, and everything you have written here goes: answers, photos, voice notes, comments, reactions, and suggested questions. Rounds that already went out will no longer show anything from you. It cannot be undone.
leave.otherLoops: This only affects {groupName}. If you are in other loops, each has its own link.
leave.confirmLabel: I understand everything I wrote in {groupName} will be deleted
leave.ownerBody: An owner can't leave through their link. Sign in and hand the loop to one of its admins, or delete the loop from its settings.
leave.confirmError: Tick the box to confirm. Nothing was deleted.

goodbye.title: It's all gone.
goodbye.body: Everything you wrote has been deleted, along with your photos and voice notes. Copies of emails that already reached people's inboxes are theirs, and we can't recall those.

export.personalNote: Everything you wrote on Friendloop, as of exportedAt. Photos and voice notes are links; they keep working until you delete your account or leave the loop, or the loop is deleted, so save any you want to keep first.
export.loopNote: The whole loop as of exportedAt: every round with its questions, sent answers, sections, comments, and reactions. Photos and voice notes are links; they stop working once the loop or the person who added them is deleted, so save any you want to keep first. Drafts nobody has sent are not included.

privacy.title: What we keep, and why
privacy.intro: Friendloop is a small private newsletter for groups of friends. It keeps what it needs to send your loop's questions and put your answers in front of the people you chose, and nothing else. There are no ads, no tracking, and nothing is sold.

sections.heading: What we store
items: Your email address, and the name you give. If you sign in, the timezone your browser reports, so deadlines read in your own clock.
For each loop you are in: your name there, your profile photo if you add one, your role, your reminder choice, and the private link that lets you answer without an account.

Everything you write: answers (saved as drafts while you type, and shared once you send them), poll picks, photos, voice notes, section answers and music links, comments, reactions, and questions you suggest.
Birthdays and dates the loop's owner adds to its calendar.
A copy of every email we send, and delivery notices from our email provider (sent, bounced, and so on), so a failed send can be retried and never doubled.
Notes you send with the feedback button, with the page you were on, your screen size, and your browser.
One cookie when you sign in, which keeps you signed in for 30 days. Your light or dark choice is kept in your own browser.

sections.heading: Who can see it
paragraphs: The people in your loop see the answers you send, your name and photo, your comments and reactions, once the round is delivered. The owner and admins also see members' email addresses and who has answered so far. Drafts are visible to nobody but you.
If the loop's owner turns on share links, anyone holding a round's share link can read that round. They are off unless the owner turns them on, and the owner can replace them at any time.
Photos and voice notes are stored at long, unguessable web addresses. Anyone given one of those addresses can open that file.

sections.heading: Services that handle it for us
paragraphs: We use a few companies to run Friendloop. Each one handles your data only to do its job for us. Their servers may be outside your country.
items: Vercel runs the website and stores photos and voice notes (Vercel Blob).
Neon hosts the database where everything else lives.
Resend sends our emails, so it sees each recipient's address and the email itself.
Sentry receives error reports when something breaks, which can include the page address, your browser, and technical details of the failure.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Everything stays until it is deleted: by you, or by the loop's owner deleting the loop. When something is deleted it is removed from the database straight away, and its photos and voice notes are removed from storage moments later (if storage is briefly unavailable, we keep retrying).

Our database provider keeps a short recovery history for a limited time, so deleted data can linger there for a few days before it ages out. Emails that already reached someone's inbox belong to them, and we can't recall them; our own stored copies of sent emails that name you are blanked when you delete your data.

sections.heading: Taking it with you, and deleting it
items: Signed in: open Your loops and use Download my data for a file of everything you have written, or Delete my account to remove your account and all of it, in every loop.
Only using the link in your email: at the bottom of the answer page, Leave this loop removes you from that loop and deletes everything you wrote there. You can download it first.
Owners can download a whole loop, and delete it, from the loop's settings. If you own a loop that has other people in it, hand it to one of its admins or delete it before deleting your account.
If an owner removes you from a loop, you stop getting its emails, but what you already wrote stays until you delete it.

terms.title: The ground rules
terms.intro: Friendloop is free, open source, and run for groups of friends. By using it you agree to these terms. They are short on purpose.

sections.heading: Your words stay yours
paragraphs: You own what you write and upload. You let us store it, and show it to the people in your loop (and to anyone the owner shares a round with), only so Friendloop can do its job. That permission ends when you delete it.

sections.heading: Be a good friend
items: Only invite people who would want to be invited, and only add your own photos and recordings, or ones you have permission to share.
Nothing illegal, hateful, or harassing, and nothing that exposes someone else's private information.
Don't try to get into loops you weren't invited to, overload the service, or get around its limits.
You need to be at least 13, and old enough where you live to agree to these terms.

sections.heading: Owners
paragraphs: The owner of a loop decides who is in it, which questions it asks, whether rounds can be shared by link, and whether it keeps going. Owners can remove people and can delete the whole loop, with everything in it.

sections.heading: No guarantees
paragraphs: Friendloop is provided as it is, without warranties. We work to keep it running and your words safe, but emails can be late, things can break, and we may change or stop the service. Keep your own copy of anything you can't bear to lose: Download my data is there for that.
As far as the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for what other people in your loop write.

sections.heading: When things go wrong
paragraphs: We may remove content or close an account that breaks these terms. You can stop using Friendloop and delete your data at any time. If these terms change in a way that matters, we will say so before the change applies.
